links.outcome: Reading ease and readability of original vs ChatGPT-simplified responses to breast cancer questions
links.effect: Mean reading ease improved from 46 to 70 (P<.001); readability from grade 13 to 8.9 (P<.001); all 25 simplified responses met reading ease criteria, but only 2 of 25 (8%) met sixth-grade readability.
links.quote: ChatGPT improved mean reading ease (original responses, 46 vs simplified responses, 70; P < .001) and readability (original, grade 13 vs simplified, grade 8.9; P < .001) and decreased word count (original, 193 vs simplified, 173; P < .001).

links.outcome: Reading level of original ChatGPT responses relative to sixth-grade target
links.effect: Original responses averaged grade 13 readability and only 2 of 25 had adequate reading ease; simplified responses still averaged grade 8.9, with only 2 of 25 (8%) meeting sixth-grade readability.
links.quote: Two of the 25 simplified responses (8%) met criteria for adequate readability.

links.effect: 92% (23 of 25) of simplified responses were clinically appropriate, so 2 of 25 contained inappropriate content, which the authors say necessitates physician oversight.
links.quote: Ninety-two percent (23 of 25) of simplified responses were considered clinically appropriate.

unlisted_practices: Using an LLM to simplify existing patient education content to a target reading level
